newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares pause after recent heady gains.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares pause after recent heady gains.

text.p: Leading Russian shares were little changed on Monday and traders forecast possible stagnation for the rest of the month after recent heady gains.
The Russian Trading System of 22 leading shares edged down by 0.05 percent to 355.46 on $24.93 million in total market volume.

"I am afraid the situation testifies to the fact that blue chips will be unchanged for the whole of June -- I can see no reason for a price jump and investors are unwilling to sell big packages," a Western investment company trader said.
"That's why the market is in for a stagnation period with periodical rises in undervalued less liqiud paper."
Regional power utility Novosibirskenergo NVNG.RTS rose to $8.85 from $7.25 on May 28, when it was last traded.
Traders said foreign buyers were showing only patchy interest in leading shares.
But Renaissance Capital trader Vladimir Chkhikvadze said there was support on practically all of the most liquid shares.

"Although the blue chips market is sagging, there is a certain and quite powerful support -- that's why even in our volatile market, a falling trend in the chips will not cause a (total market) fall of more than one percent," he said.
National power utility UES EESR.RTS fell to $0.3138 from $0.3170 at Friday's close, while Mosenergo MSNG.RTS edged up to $1.279 from $1.263.
Surgutneftegaz SNGS.RTS ordinary shares fell to $0.8500 from $0.8625, preferred shares SNGS_p.RTS edged down to $0.548 from $0.552.
NK Surgut, of which Surgutnegtegaz is the main crude oil production unit, decided last week to limit all investors, foreign and domestic, to one percent of voting shares.
Traders said Surgutneftegaz preferreds saw lively trade.
